title: Sources of Error
content:
1. Backlash error in the travelling microscope screw, if the direction of motion is reversed mid-measurement.

2. Imperfect point contact between the lens and plate (due to dust or a slightly flattened lens surface), which causes a systematic diameter offset — largely cancelled out by the differential (D²(n+m) − D²(n)) method, but not entirely if severe.

3. Non-monochromatic or impure sodium light, if the lamp has not fully warmed up and stabilized.

4. Parallax error while reading the vernier scale.

5. An incorrect independently-measured value of R, which directly and linearly affects the final wavelength — this is one of the most common causes of a very large percentage error.

6. An inconsistent or incorrectly computed least count applied across different readings.

7. Eccentricity of the rings due to a lens surface imperfection, causing asymmetry between the left-hand and right-hand readings.
keywords: why is my percentage error large
